scenes.say: The least skilled person in the room is often the most confident. There's a study for that.
The Dunning-Kruger effect: lacking a skill also means lacking the skill to notice.
scenes.show: You can't see what you lack.

scenes.say: Kruger and Dunning tested people in 1999. The bottom group scored around the {actual}th percentile.
They rated themselves around the {self}nd percentile. Above average.
The skill you need to do something well is the same skill you need to see you're doing it badly.
If a field looks too easy, you probably haven't seen how hard it is yet.
